title: Custom hooks
canDo: extract reusable logic into custom hooks

blocks.md: You've got a `useState` + `useEffect` pair that syncs a value to `localStorage`. It works great in your settings panel — so you copy-paste it into your profile page, then again into the theme picker. Three copies of the same logic, three places to fix the next bug. React has a better answer: **custom hooks**. Extract once, use everywhere.

blocks.canDo: extract reusable logic into custom hooks
blocks.md: By the end of this session you will be able to: recognise when stateful logic is duplicated across components, extract it into a custom hook, and explain why the `use` prefix is required.

Work through **Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks** on react.dev. It walks through building `useOnlineStatus` and `useChatRoom` from scratch, explains exactly when extraction is and isn't worth it, and covers the mental model of hooks as event synchronisers.
blocks.label: Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks — react.dev

blocks.md: **Come back here once you've finished the resource.** The quiz below takes about 5 minutes and locks in the three things that trip people up most.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a custom hook?
options: A built-in React API you import from 'react'
A JavaScript function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other hooks inside it
A component that wraps other components to share state
A higher-order function that returns a component
questions.explanation: A custom hook is just a plain JavaScript function with a `use` prefix that can call other hooks — no special API required.

questions.question: Why must a custom hook's name start with `use`?
options: React will throw an error at runtime if the name is wrong
It is a naming convention with no technical effect
The linter uses the prefix to enforce the Rules of Hooks inside that function
It makes the function available as a JSX element
questions.explanation: The `use` prefix tells the React linter that this function may call hooks, so it enforces hook rules (call order, no conditionals) inside it. Skip the prefix and those checks are silently skipped.

questions.question: Two components both call `useLocalStorage('theme', 'light')`. What do they share?
options: The same state — updating one automatically updates the other
Nothing — custom hooks cannot be called more than once
The same logic but independent state — each component has its own state value
The same state only if they are siblings in the component tree
questions.explanation: Custom hooks share logic, not state. Every call to a custom hook creates its own isolated state. To share state between components you still need to lift it up or use context.

blocks.md:
**What you covered:**

- A custom hook is a `use`-prefixed function that calls other hooks — nothing more.
- The `use` prefix activates linter enforcement of the Rules of Hooks inside the function.
- Custom hooks share *logic*, not *state* — each call site gets independent state.
- Classic extraction trigger: the same `useState` + `useEffect` pattern appearing in more than one component.
bullets: Custom hook = `use`-prefixed function that calls hooks
The `use` prefix is required — the linter relies on it
Each component that calls a custom hook gets its own state
Extract when you see duplicated useState+useEffect combos
